bottom_line: In CHARM-Added, candesartan vs placebo added to ACE inhibitors reduced the primary outcome of cardiovascular death or hospital admission for CHF (unadjusted hazard ratio 0.85 [95% CI 0.75–0.96]).
implications: These data support that, in this population on ACE inhibitors, adding candesartan reduced the risk of the composite of cardiovascular death or hospital admission for CHF versus placebo (hazard ratio 0.85 [95% CI 0.75–0.96]). The report also shows higher rates of permanent discontinuation for adverse events/laboratory abnormalities with candesartan (309 [24.2] vs 233 [18.3]).

major_points.text: Randomised, double-blind trial comparing candesartan vs matching placebo in patients with CHF and reduced LVEF on ACE inhibitors.
major_points.quote: We randomly assigned patients, in a double-blind way, candesartan or matching placebo

major_points.text: Enrolled 2548 patients with NYHA class II–IV CHF and LVEF 40% or lower who were being treated with ACE inhibitors.
major_points.quote: we enrolled 2548 patients with New York Heart Association functional class II–IV CHF and left-ventricular ejection fraction 40% or lower, and who were being treated with ACE inhibitors.

major_points.text: Primary outcome was cardiovascular death or unplanned admission to hospital for worsening CHF.
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was cardiovascular death or unplanned admission to hospital for the management of worsening CHF.

major_points.text: Primary outcome occurred in 483 (38%) vs 538 (42%) with hazard ratio 0.85 (95% CI 0.75–0.96).
major_points.quote: 483 (38%) patients in the candesartan group and 538 (42%) in the placebo group experienced the primary outcome (unadjusted hazard ratio 0·85 [95% CI 0·75–0·96], p=0·011

major_points.text: Analysis was intention-to-treat and used time-to-first-event methods (logrank; Cox regression with prespecified covariates).
major_points.quote: Analysis was done by intention to treat.

harms.text: Permanent discontinuation because of adverse event or abnormal lab value was more frequent with candesartan.
harms.quote:
Overall, 309 (24%) patients in the candesartan group and
     233 (18%) patients in the placebo group permanently
     discontinued study medication because of an adverse event
     or an abnormal laboratory value (p=0·0003, table 4).

harms.text: Increase in creatinine leading to discontinuation was more frequent with candesartan (7.8 vs 4.1).
Hyperkalaemia leading to discontinuation was more frequent with candesartan (3.4 vs 0.7).
Two cases of angioedema in candesartan and three in placebo; two required hospital admission.
